recent_posts.title: Inside High-Frequency Trading Systems: The Race to Zero Latency
recent_posts.summary: Explores the architecture of high-frequency trading systems that operate at microsecond and nanosecond speeds. Covers market data ingestion using kernel-bypass frameworks like DPDK, in-memory order book implementations with lock-free data structures, FPGA-based hardware acceleration for tick-to-trade execution, event-driven architectures with nanosecond-precision timestamps, smart order routing, and pre-trade risk checks. Demonstrates how every component from network cards to silicon logic is optimized to minimize latency in financial trading systems.

recent_posts.title: SwiftUI FocusState: A Little Pitfall I Fall Into
recent_posts.summary: Explores a common SwiftUI gotcha where FocusState only updates to true when the bound TextField is already visible on screen. The author demonstrates the problem through a practical example of trying to conditionally show a TextField based on its focus state, which creates a catch-22 situation. The solution involves using a separate State variable to control TextField visibility, synchronized with FocusState through onChange modifiers.

recent_posts.title: How to Scale Like a Senior Engineer (Servers, DBs, LBs, SPOFs)
recent_posts.summary: Scaling systems is about solving problems incrementally, not jumping to complex solutions. Start with understanding single server limitations, identify bottlenecks (CPU, memory, disk I/O), then make informed decisions about vertical vs horizontal scaling. Database optimization is often the real bottleneck, not application servers. Load balancers require careful algorithm selection and configuration. Even redundant architectures have single points of failure that need identification and mitigation. The key is adding complexity only when necessary and understanding the tradeoffs at each step.

recent_posts.title: SwiftUI: Render/Animate Geometries With Metal 4
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to rendering and animating geometric shapes using Metal 4 in SwiftUI. Covers the fundamentals of Metal's rendering pipeline, including vertex and fragment shaders, command buffers, and render encoders. Demonstrates how to draw a simple line with gradient colors and add rotation animation by passing parameters to shaders. Includes detailed explanations of Metal framework classes, buffer management, and the complete workflow from vertex processing to screen presentation.

recent_posts.title: SwiftUI: LongPressGesture OnChange Not triggered! Updating Not triggered!
recent_posts.summary: Explores common issues with SwiftUI's LongPressGesture when trying to track press state changes. The onChanged callback doesn't trigger when minimumDuration is 0, and the updating callback has similar limitations. The solution involves using the onLongPressGesture modifier with onPressingChanged parameter, which works reliably even with zero minimum duration.

recent_posts.title: BigQuery Advanced Runtime: Testing Performance Part 1
recent_posts.summary: BigQuery's new Advanced Runtime automatically improves query performance by up to 30% through enhanced vectorization without requiring code changes. Testing with TPC-H dataset showed runtime reduction from 398s to 280s and 32% decrease in slot consumption, translating to significant cost savings for slot-based pricing models. The feature can be enabled with a simple ALTER PROJECT command and provides immediate benefits for analytical workloads.

recent_posts.title: Understanding embeddings and vector similarity for AI applications
recent_posts.summary: Embeddings are numerical vector representations that transform text, images, and code into dense vectors capturing semantic meaning and relationships. The article explains how embeddings work through tokenization and neural network encoding, demonstrates similarity measurement using cosine similarity, and showcases practical applications including semantic search, recommendations, clustering, and RAG systems. It features the Qodo-Embed-1 model as a real-world example and provides Python code examples for implementing various embedding-based tasks.

recent_posts.title: 🔧 Improving Modular Architecture in Swift iOS Projects
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to implementing modular architecture in Swift iOS projects, covering feature-based module organization, dependency management, interface design, and testing strategies. The post provides practical patterns including builders/factories for module instantiation, coordinator patterns for navigation, and tools like Swift Package Manager and Tuist for dependency management. It emphasizes creating clear module boundaries, avoiding cross-feature coupling, and maintaining testable, scalable codebases through proper abstraction and dependency injection.

recent_posts.title: Understanding derivedStateOf in Jetpack Compose : Optimize your recompositions
recent_posts.summary: derivedStateOf is a Jetpack Compose optimization tool that prevents unnecessary recalculations during recompositions. It caches derived values and only recalculates them when their actual dependencies change, not on every UI update. The function works by creating a DerivedSnapshotState object that tracks input states and maintains cached results. This is particularly useful for expensive operations like complex validations, regex processing, or calculations that would otherwise run on every recomposition, improving app performance significantly.

recent_posts.title: Building an AI food visualization service with OCR and image generation APIs
recent_posts.summary: A developer built an AI-powered food visualization service in a weekend that converts menu text descriptions into realistic food images. The system uses a three-step pipeline: Tesseract.js extracts text from menu photos, OpenAI's GPT structures the raw text into dish descriptions, and Replicate's Stable Diffusion generates photorealistic food images. The full-stack application uses React/TypeScript for the frontend, Python Flask for the backend, and is containerized with Docker for easy deployment across platforms like Render, Railway, and Vercel.
